falsifier: The build was tested against: (1) does every tab render on template-city AND empty-city with no console errors on the DEPLOYED revision, not just locally; (2) does the free-text description field render anywhere in a list, and can a permanent regression test catch its return; (3) do the interactive controls (search, filters, pager, load strip, view modes, attention-row navigation) actually work when driven by a real browser, not just assert markup shape. All three falsifiers were run for real (headless Chromium against both the local dev server and the live production URL) and none of them broke the build -- the build passed by surviving genuine attempts to break it, not by construction.
contradicted: Two things this lane's own early assumptions got wrong, corrected in-session: (1) CP1 initially assumed no domain-layer work was needed (data layer + basic renderer already existed); this held for four of five domains but Work orders and Code enforcement needed a NEW managerLoad/officerLoad extra added to their domain modules, since the load component the mission asks for had no data to read. (2) This lane's own attention-row implementation (a small <a class="go"> link line inside a plain .metric div) was itself a divergent second implementation of a UI pattern a concurrent lane (G-120) had already built, hardened through a real CI accessibility failure, and merged -- discovered only at rebase. Reworked onto G-120's established pattern rather than shipping the divergence.
leave_behind: OPEN FINDING for the operator or a lane with real PDF/image access: the dispatch's per-tab metric-strip/filter category names for Pipeline ('active, requested, expired, expiring, pending docs, on hold') and Work orders ('active, requested, suspended, on hold, archived') do not match the already-shipped, tested status vocabulary in src/adapters.mjs. Real, concurrent, independent evidence for Work orders specifically (the approved mockup's own status pills read 'Active'/'Suspended'/'On hold'; src/mygov-live.mjs's mapRealWorkOrderRecord() already passes the live feed's raw status through unmapped; G-120's own Overview tile links to Pipeline with filter=active). Not changed here: rewriting the core status enum is a breaking change to a widely-tested contract, and SmartCity OS Screenshots (1).pdf could not be rendered in this tool environment (pdftoppm/poppler-utils unavailable) to confirm the true vendor vocabulary. Full detail in CP2.

Pipeline's 'All/Active/Requested/Expired/Expiring/Pending docs/On hold' filter list and Work orders' 'Year'/'All departments' dropdowns from the approved mockup were simplified to the shared search+status+reset pattern (plus each tab's own named extra selects) given scope/time -- a stated simplification, not a silent gap.

Pagination and filtering are client-side (the full record set is fetched once via the existing /api/domains/:id route, sliced in the browser). Correct for template-city; for a real grant at Bastrop's volumes (16,723 work orders, 12,683 pipeline cases) this means one large JSON response per tab load. Could not be measured against real data because G-122 (the live v1 API regression) makes Bastrop reads unavailable to test against right now. A real scaling question for whoever owns this lens next.
Work orders' Map view mode renders an honest not-built state: the shared map component is G-121/G-124's pinned, held work, and building a second one here would have been scope creep into a HELD row.

The escalation-ladder register panel and the code-enforcement case-load stats panel that G-97's build carried are not present in the redesigned Code enforcement tab -- deliberately cut as redundant with the new tier-3 metric strip (which now carries a Total tile) and the officer load strip, consistent with 'three tiers, not two walls of numbers.' Stated here since it is content removal, not purely additive.

record.comments (the live inspections feed's raw free-text field) still transits the /api/domains/inspections JSON response for an authenticated tenant caller -- not rendered by any surface (permanently asserted by a regression test), but still on the wire, inspectable via browser devtools by anyone with real Bastrop tenant access. Building a data-layer gate for this is explicitly named as separate, future work in the design README, not this lane's scope.
missionPremise: The approved design (https://claude.ai/code/artifact/1ed0733e-e10c-4ec6-948e-66d2b24e562e, _design/smartcity-dev-services/README.md) replaces v1's two-walls-of-numbers pattern with a three-tier hierarchy (attention row, tab-strip counts, compact metric strip), replaces per-tab bespoke row layouts with one table treatment, consolidates three load panels into one component, and turns the free-text description into something that is never a list column -- because v1's captured descriptions carry citizen names and phone numbers verbatim. The data layer for all five domains (G-92) and a basic four-state renderer (G-97) already existed on origin/main at dispatch time; this lane's actual job was the visual/interaction redesign onto the new pattern, not new data plumbing, discovered by reading the existing codebase before writing any code rather than assumed from the dispatch text alone.
completionPredicate: All five tabs (Pipeline, Inspections, Work orders, Code enforcement, Licences) render the approved three-tier pattern with the approved column set, on the DEPLOYED production revision, verified live against both template-city and empty-city with a real browser (not just unit tests asserting markup shape); the free-text description renders in no list column on any tab, and a permanent regression test asserts record.comments is never read by any renderer; the four CSS gates (no colour/token in shell.css, sc-kit.css untouched, 12px floor / type ramp intact, no unstyled class) are green; CI (test + the required a11y accessibility job) reports the conclusion string SUCCESS on the merge commit; the PR is merged; the canary was verified on its own URL before any traffic moved to it; the traffic shift was verified by reading the Cloud Run traffic JSON by field name, never a positional formatter.
scopeBasis: Place (G-124) and Plan review (separate scope, operator ruling 2026-09-14) are excluded because they are explicitly HELD/out-of-scope in this row's own dispatch; both render their honest not-built state with a stated basis rather than a blank, and Plan review/Flood study were added to the tab strip as named-but-not-built per the dispatch's explicit instruction ('a tab named in the strip but not built renders the honest not-built state'). The status-vocabulary rewrite is excluded because it is a breaking change to a separately-owned, widely-tested contract that this lane could not verify against the cited source material in this tool environment -- reported as an open finding rather than guessed at, consistent with 'do not remap onto an invented taxonomy.' The core map component (Work orders' Map view mode) is excluded because it is G-121/G-124's pinned, held work and building a second one would have duplicated rather than shared it.

piiCodePathsFound.path: src/mygov-permits.mjs mapRealPermitRecord() subject construction -> web/app.js pipelineRow()
piiCodePathsFound.description: CONFIRMED LATENT and FIXED. subject: row.title || row.description || row.type fell back to the free-text description field when a real permit lacked a title, and pipelineRow() renders record.subject directly. Fixed: the '|| row.description' link removed from the fallback chain; a permit with neither a title nor a type now states an absence ('Untitled permit') rather than reaching for the free-text field. Whether any real Bastrop permit row actually lacks a title (making this reachable in practice before the fix) could not be verified live -- G-122 makes Bastrop reads unavailable to test against right now.

CONFIRMED LATENT and FIXED. Same fallback shape as the permits case (subject: row.type || row.description). Was masked by an unrelated bug (codeViolationRow() read the nonexistent record.violationType rather than record.subject on real data, so the fallback never actually reached the screen) rather than by design -- fixing the column mapping without also removing the fallback would have made this live. Both fixed together: the fallback removed, and the new codeViolationRow() reads record.violationType (fixture) or falls back to a stated absence, never record.subject's free-text-capable chain.
